## Two files, two clocks {#clocks data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="ck" id="ck">
  <div class="sm-controls">
    <div class="sm-mode ck-mode" role="group" aria-label="Hours added to the analyzer timestamps">
      <button type="button" data-h="0" aria-pressed="true">Plain merge</button>
      <button type="button" data-h="1" aria-pressed="false">+1 h</button>
      <button type="button" data-h="2" aria-pressed="false">+2 h</button>
      <button type="button" data-h="3" aria-pressed="false">+3 h</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <svg id="ck-plot" viewBox="0 0 1160 360" role="img" aria-label="Sensor and analyzer over three days, with the analyzer timestamps shifted"></svg>
  <p class="sm-readout" id="ck-out" aria-live="polite"></p>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ck'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  // Real data, 13 to 15 September 2004 (UCI Air Quality), Lab 07 Demo A. sens: PT08.S1(CO), local time.
  // benz: C6H6(GT), local time, with 6 hours before and after; the analyzer file stamps it in UTC (local minus 2 h).
  const D = {"sens":[1038,934,900,870,875,940,1053,1509,1559,1313,1372,1320,1346,1307,1157,1154,1172,1241,1379,1570,1418,1317,1204,1014,956,891,856,863,911,936,1087,1540,1513,1409,1219,1286,1228,1140,1052,1282,1378,1506,1310,1204,1071,967,947,1011,971,886,908,901,915,940,1048,1298,1487,1327,1363,1393,1361,1289,1265,1339,1269,1299,1546,1571,1312,1074,1127,1040],"benz":[8,12.6,17.5,14.8,23.3,12.2,7.2,4.6,3.8,3.7,4,5.5,8.3,28.2,32.1,17.7,18.4,16.3,18.2,17.9,12.6,11.3,14.9,18.5,25.2,35.9,26.7,19.9,14.6,6.9,5.6,3.9,3.2,3.9,4.6,5,9.6,27.8,32.1,20.9,11.8,15.8,15.8,14,8.2,13.7,19.5,26.7,18.7,13.9,6.7,4.2,3.6,4.4,4.2,2.6,3.1,3,3.4,4,7.8,16.1,27.6,17.8,18.5,21.6,21,17.2,16.1,18.6,17.2,17.3,28.6,31.8,20.1,9.2,10.3,8.6,8.6,4.8,2.6,4.3,4.5,6.6],"scan":[[-2,0.17],[-1,0.32],[0,0.54],[1,0.78],[2,0.93],[3,0.79],[4,0.57]]};
  const W = 1160, H = 360, L = 70, R = 70, T = 16, B = 46, n = D.sens.length;
  const X = (j) => L + j / (n - 1) * (W - L - R), VB = (v) => T + (1 - v / 40) * (H - T - B), VS = (v) => T + (1 - (v - 700) / 1000) * (H - T - B);
  const DAY = ['Mon 13 Sep', 'Tue 14 Sep', 'Wed 15 Sep'];
  function path(vals, Y, attr) { let d = '', pen = false; vals.forEach((v, j) => { if (v === null) { pen = false; return; } d += (pen ? 'L' : 'M') + X(j).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(v).toFixed(1); pen = true; }); return `<path d="${d}" fill="none" ${attr}/>`; }
  function draw(h) {
    let g = '';
    [0, 10, 20, 30, 40].forEach((v) => { g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${VB(v)}" y2="${VB(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${VB(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="16" fill="#0F6E6B">${v}</text>`; });
    [800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600].forEach((v) => { g += `<text x="${W - R + 10}" y="${VS(v) + 6}" font-size="16" fill="#9a5f10">${v}</text>`; });
    for (let d = 0; d < 3; d++) g += `<line x1="${X(d * 24)}" x2="${X(d * 24)}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#B9C1C6" stroke-dasharray="3 4"/><text x="${X(d * 24 + 12)}" y="${H - B + 24}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${DAY[d]}</text>`;
    g += `<text transform="translate(20 ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(-90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#0F6E6B">analyzer benzene, µg/m³</text><text transform="translate(${W - 12} ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#9a5f10">sensor response</text>`;
    const shifted = D.sens.map((_, j) => D.benz[j + 6 + 2 - h]);
    g += path(D.sens, VS, 'stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="2.5"') + path(shifted, VB, 'stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="2.5"');
    document.getElementById('ck-plot').innerHTML = g;
    const r = D.scan.find((s) => s[0] === h)[1];
    document.getElementById('ck-out').textContent = h === 0
      ? `The plain merge: each sensor hour is paired with the analyzer two hours later. The peaks do not line up. Over 28 days, r = ${r}.`
      : `Analyzer timestamps plus ${h} h. ${h === 2 ? 'The peaks line up: the analyzer file was in UTC.' : 'Closer, but the peaks still do not line up.'} Over 28 days, r = ${r}.`;
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-h]').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', Number(b.dataset.h) === h));
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-h]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => draw(Number(b.dataset.h))));
  draw(0);
})();
</script>
```

[Lab 07, Demo A: sensor PT08.S1(CO) and benzene C6H6(GT), 13 to 15 September 2004. Data: De Vito, UCI Air Quality, doi:10.24432/C59K5F, CC BY 4.0.]{.source}

[Pairs · 10 minutes · no computer needed]{.act-label}

<div class="stories" id="first">

  <div class="story"><p>The lab assay is taken once a day at about 09:00. The sensor logs every minute.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Join the slow to the fast:</b> the sensor value nearest the sample time (pandas merge_asof), or its mean over the sampling window.</p></div>

  <div class="story"><p>After a network outage the logger re-sent its buffer. Some rows appear twice.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Repeated rows:</b> count them and drop exact duplicates before a merge copies them.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>On 31 October the 02:00 hour appears twice; on 28 March there is no 02:00.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>Daylight saving.</b> Store in UTC, convert only for display.</p></div>
  <div class="story"><p>A flow meter reads exactly 41.2 for nine hours.</p><button type="button">Reveal</button><p class="ans" hidden><b>A stuck value,</b> not a steady plant. Treat as missing after checking the log (Lab 03).</p></div>
</div>

(function () {

</script>

For each file: what is the problem, what would it do to the result if missed, and which check finds it?

## The path to a decision {#path}

| Step | The question | Week |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Audit | What is in each file: rows, codes for missing, repeated rows, the clock? | 1 |
| Clean | Which values are missing, and which are impossible? Fill only what you can defend. | 2, 3 |
| Align | Do the two files mean the same hour? Check with a lag scan. | 5, 7 |
| Analyze | Calibrate on one period, test on another. Compare with what ordinary periods give. | 5, 6 |
| Decide | State the decision, the numbers, what you did to the data, and the limits. | 4, 7 |

[An error in an early step does not show as an error later. It shows as a confident wrong number.]{.note-line}

## Activity 2 · Lab 07, Steps 1 to 3 {#act2 .activity}

[Individual · 25 minutes · laptop or phone]{.act-label}

1. Open **Lab 07** and enter your name and student ID. Press **My data set**.
2. Step 2: read the first rows of both raw files and write two things you would check before merging.
3. Step 3: predict whether the sensor will flag at least 80 % of the hours above 15 µg/m³.
4. Do not audit or align yet. Download your study in Step 10 to keep your work.
